newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Novosibirsk repays munis with 2-day delay.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Novosibirsk repays munis with 2-day delay.

text.p: The Novosibirsk regional administration repaid a 4.60 billion rouble KODO municipal bond issue two days after it was due with a penalty for the delay, an administration official said on Friday.
"We made the repayment at face value and, besides, we paid the penalty of 80 percent annual to all market participants," Alexei Volkov, finance and tax policy department deputy head told Reuters.
On Wednesday, the Novosibirsk administration failed to repay the 4.60 billion rouble KODO issue and suspended secondary trading until the issue was repaid.
The administration blamed the delay on unpaid taxes.
It also cancelled a KODO auction of three billion roubles on Wednesday.
Volkov said the administration was working out extra measures to guarantee bond issues.
"I am sure, we shall have no more delays in repaying other KODO issues," he said. "It was a technical break, but it taught the administration a good lesson."
Alexander Kaml, head of the administration finance department, said it would soon set up an extra system of guarantees for the KODO market.
This would allow investors to be compensated at the central bank's refinancing rate, currently 80 percent, on the day payments are delayed.
The administration was considering using a banking credit line as an extra guarantee.
Volkov said the guarantee system was likely to be approved for a new KODO issue of at least 120 billion roubles. The issue date has not yet been set, he said.
